coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers

coverage.found: No dedicated search (budget). The only Lebanese signal is the jeweller/AML angle already in K02.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K02. BDL Basic Circular 6 (article dated 28 Aug 2026) lists buying, selling and shipping precious metals among money-changer services. No separate gold-dealer licence found. Lebanon is still on the FATF grey list per al-Modon.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No Lebanese dismantler or scrapping rule found. The only vehicle-linked results were mechanical inspection (cat. 18) and uninspected used-car imports (Annahar, 25,000+ cars in 2024).

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: Animal Welfare Law 47/2017 covers animal transport, with 15+ implementing decrees still expected; no evidence they were issued. No register or reporting duty confirmed. Beirut port is the main livestock entry point (WOAH document).

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: No Lebanese abattoir licensing text found. Food Safety Law 35/2015 sets record-keeping and licensing duties for all food businesses. Implementation lags: the Food Safety Authority board was first appointed by Decision 50 on 24 Oct 2025 (FAO via search summary). Implementing decrees not found.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Nothing found for Lebanon in one combined search. Unverified.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Search for the veterinary syndicate and veterinary pharmacy licensing returned only Jordan, Egypt and Idlib. No Lebanese vet-medicine register rule found. Ministry of Agriculture Animal Resources Directorate is the competent authority. Unverified.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Energy and Water Ministry publishes an application form for a licence to drill a non-artesian well. The copies found date from 2016. Needs the army geographic-department coordinate certificate and a drilling-company undertaking. No periodic reporting duty found.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Law 80/2018 and decrees 5605/2019 (source separation) and 5606/2019 (hazardous waste) exist. No licence regime for sludge or septic haulers found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: No Lebanese lift or boiler inspection decree found; results were only Israel, Malta and Cyprus. Unverified.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Water Establishments Law 221 covers regional establishments. No licensing text for water tankers or small private suppliers found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: Ministry of Agriculture resolutions 392/1/2003, 280/1/2004, 49/1/2004, 52/1/2009 and 310/1/2010 cover registration, import and control of agricultural pesticides (FAOLEX; not repealed). No dealer register or reporting duty found, and no 2025-26 update. Unverified.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Domestic-worker recruitment agencies are regulated by Ministry of Labour Decision 74/1 of 1 Jul 2025. A minister's memo of 26 Dec 2025 bans all agency advertising, including WhatsApp, with labour inspection to enforce it. In Feb 2026 Minister Mohammad Haidar cancelled the annual prior approvals given to each agency, and the agencies' syndicate objected. Opportunity candidate logged.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Nothing found for Lebanon. Unverified.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: About 13,000 associations, with about 700 new each year (Annahar). They are registered by notification (ilm wa khabar) under the 1909 law at the Interior Ministry. They are expected to submit year-end income and expenditure, but the ministry cannot enforce this. BDL Circular 170 (14 Jul 2025) bars banks and financial institutions from dealing with unlicensed associations. Candidate logged.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Annahar (Oct 2025) estimates about 20,000 taxis, 15,000 buses and 10,000 vans run on forged public plates. New smart plates and a new Traffic Law (first phase from 22 April) are being phased in. Official tariff signed by Works and Transport Minister Rassamni. A 12M LBP per month stipend is planned for public drivers for Oct-Dec 2026, conditional on complying with the tariff, with a joint Finance and Works decision still to come. Mechanical inspection centres were closed or looted. Fees are paid via OMT, Whish and similar money-transfer firms (2024).

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05, but new rule evidence. BDL Basic Circular 6 (Governor Karim Souaid; al-Modon article dated 28 Aug 2026) sets licensing categories A1, A, A2 and B. Minimum capital is LBP 25bn, 100bn, 25bn and 10bn respectively, held in a frozen BDL account. At least two-thirds of ownership must be Lebanese natural persons. Existing changers reportedly get one year, renewable for 6 months, to comply. The article did not state reporting duties; the full circular was not checked. Street vendors: nothing found.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Nurseries: the Ministry of Public Health (Mother and Child) closes unlicensed day nurseries, but the source was undated and no 2025 decree was found. Driving schools: exams were halted in Oct 2022, and licences are issued per district. In March 2026 the state issued 18 licences, covering schools, weapons-import firms and sports centres, and was defining licensing rules for fitness clubs (Policy Initiative). Food producers: see cat. 7. Tattoo and hunting: nothing found.

coverage.found: Only bread and flour price and supply news: the Economy Ministry set the bread bundle at LBP 70,000 in March 2026, and an inter-ministerial wheat and flour distribution committee exists (undated). No bakery or mill register or recurring report found. Weak lead only.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: Agricultural co-ops register with the Directorate General of Co-operatives (Ministry of Agriculture); registration is a UNDP grant condition. The Policy Initiative March 2026 summary says 29 co-ops and mutual funds were dissolved. No recurring filing duty found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: Documented insurer payment delays (2-3 months) and NSSF tariff and reimbursement disputes. No e-claims platform or mandated billing format found. Unverified gap for small clinics and labs, mostly a reconciliation problem.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Domestic-worker recruitment offices are now governed by Labour Ministry decision 74/1 of 1/7/2025, and a 26/12/2025 memo bans their advertising, including on WhatsApp. Nothing found on private security or cleaning company licensing, so that part is unverified.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Quarry sector is under Decree 8803 and the National Quarries Council. April 2026 dispute: the cabinet licensed cement firms without requiring payment of about USD 370.2M in dues (UNDP/Environment Ministry, 2022-23). The solar-installation joint decision is listed under 31. The quarry findings mostly concern large firms. No small-contractor register found.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K02. Lebanon is on the FATF grey list. No 2025-26 SIC (Special Investigation Commission) circular addressed to notaries or brokers surfaced. A land-registry disruption in the South and Nabatieh is noted (NRC, June 2026).

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Hotels send guest data via an electronic application linked to General Security (named by the tourism union head, app name not given). The Diyafa guest-house syndicate reminded members to report guest names and data after a Hazmieh hotel strike. Short-term rentals (Airbnb, about 10,000 rooms) have no clear legal framework. Tourism Minister Lahoud's decision gives unlicensed tourism establishments one year to comply (about May 2025 to about mid-2026, exact date unverified). No local guest-register software found.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Only the ILO / Ministry of Agriculture / Zahle chamber EU-standards certification programme for exporters, starting with cherries (April 2025). No mandatory exporter register or traceability rule found. K07 already covers customs. Unverified.

coverage.category: 31. Solar PV installation permits (country-specific)
coverage.found: Joint decision 1234 of 9/9/2026 (Interior, Public Works, Energy) set a municipal permit for solar systems under 1.5 MW, with engineer statements and a 15-day tacit approval. The Electricity Regulatory Authority said it would appeal; the Prime Minister's office then directed that the decision be set aside. The trigger is currently withdrawn.

coverage.category: 32. Sayrafa platform profit tax (country-specific)
coverage.found: 17% exceptional tax on profits from Sayrafa dollar purchases in 2021-2023. Paper declaration on form T5 at Libanpost; payment on form S18. The Finance Ministry deadline was 1 October 2026 and has passed; tax-administration audit follows. Sources conflict on the threshold (USD 15,000 vs 100,000) and on the legal article (2024 budget Art. 93 vs 2026 budget Art. 52).

coverage.category: 33. Domestic-worker recruitment offices (country-specific, Labour Ministry)
coverage.found: Decision 74/1 of 1/7/2025 governs the offices; December 2025 memo bans advertising. See ledger. Related to group A category 1.

coverage.category: 34. Health and fitness club licensing (country-specific, 2026 decree)
coverage.found: The Policy Initiative March 2026 summary says regulatory texts defined licensing requirements for health and fitness clubs. The decree number and text were not retrievable, so the details are unverified.

coverage.category: 35. Industrial licences and certificates (country-specific, Ministry of Industry)
coverage.found: The Policy Initiative March 2026 summary says industrial certificates had their validity extended. Number, scope and date were not retrievable (PDF memo was unreadable). Unverified.

coverage.category: 36. Employers of foreign workers: Egyptian workers who entered on tourist visas (country-specific)
coverage.found: A Labour Ministry agreement to regularise Egyptian workers who entered on tourist visas was reported on 28/4/2026 (maspero.eg). Details, deadline and employer duties not read. Unverified.

coverage.category: 37. Private generator operators (country-specific)
coverage.found: K04 already covers this. A search for generator tariffs and registration returned nothing current, and budget was spent elsewhere.

coverage.category: 38. Tax deadline extensions and penalty reductions, 2026 (country-specific)
coverage.found: Forvis Mazars Tax Alert 36-2026 (PDF unreadable) appears to show the Q1 2026 stamp-duty declaration moved to 15/8/2026. The Policy Initiative says penalties were cut and filing deadlines extended in March 2026. Same duty as K01, so nothing new.

candidates.evidence: Cabinet 45-day ultimatum Aug 2025 and nationwide crackdown ~30 Sep 2025 (https://www.lbcgroup.tv/news/news-bulletin-reports/881516/lbci-lebanon-articles/en); about 7,000 owners per L'Orient Today (https://today.lorientlejour.com/article/1478454/economy-minister-bisat-warns-private-generator-owners-compliance-mandatory-or-face-sanctions.html, 403 on fetch, from search snippet); 13 owners referred to prosecutors Aug 2026 (https://www.almodon.com/economy/2026/08/14/); monthly Energy Ministry tariff at https://energyandwater.gov.lb/mediafiles/prices/2-2026-02-05.doc. Competitor search in Arabic found no billing app or software for generator owners.
candidates.known_note: Same buyer and duty as K04. New evidence: meters mandatory since the Sep 2025 crackdown, monthly tariff with fixed fee plus per-kWh, active prosecution in 2026. Worth raising K04's priority.

candidates.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers

candidates.trigger: Licence to trade antiquities; sale register is plausible but unconfirmed.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: Four searches (Arabic, English, French) found no Lebanese licensing regime, police register or pawnbroker law for general second-hand dealers or pawnshops; results were from Oman, Syria, the US, Australia, France and Quebec. The only Lebanese rule found is antiquities: the 1933 antiquities order (No. 166/LR) bars trade in movable antiquities without a licence, and dealers are licensed by the Directorate General of Antiquities (source: libnanews and L'Orient Today snippets; whether it is still in force is unverified). That is a tiny, politically sensitive niche. The jeweller/gold-buyer angle stays in K02. Nothing new beyond K02; no Lebanon-specific duty found for scrap or second-hand goods.

coverage.category: 37. Private generator operators (country-specific)
coverage.found: Strong new evidence for K04. Aug 2025: cabinet gave generator owners 45 days to install individual meters and noise/emission filters and follow the Energy Ministry's monthly published tariff; the deadline passed around 30 Sep 2025; the Economy Minister said meters are 'no longer optional'. About 7,000 private generator owners are reported as affected (L'Orient Today snippet; unverified count). Enforcement: inspections by Economy Ministry consumer-protection staff with State Security in Beirut; Tripoli, Saida and Tyr municipalities seized non-compliant generators and ran them under municipal management; legal notices were issued. Aug 2026 (Al-Modon): the Economy Minister referred 13 owners to the Public Prosecution for repeated tariff violations, and diesel prices rose about 91% globally. The monthly tariff is a fixed fee per amp tier (LL385,000 for 5A, LL685,000 for 10A, LL300,000 per extra 5A) plus a per-kWh price; Aug 2026 kWh was LL48,241 (LBC snippet). So the bill formula is meter-based, which is a clean software job. No official registry app, billing platform or competitor software was found (one Arabic competitor search, nothing). Gaps: the Economy Ministry announcement page and the L'Orient articles returned 403, so exact decision numbers, records owners must keep and fine amounts are unverified. Nothing new beyond K04, but K04's trigger is now stronger than the offline pass assumed.

result.reason: Decision 74/1 (1 Jul 2025) regulating domestic-worker agencies is real, and its Art. 12 bans advertising, enforced by labour inspection (Annahar). I could not find the full text, so any recurring filing, register or contract-copy duty is unconfirmed. The ban and the cancelled approvals reduce paperwork, not add a filing. I found no Ministry portal and no competing product, but only two Arabic searches were run. Market is roughly 441 compliant of 700+ agencies in 2016, and a list of 497 registered agencies of unknown date. The syndicate has fought the Ministry's decisions in court, and agencies are a small, hostile, low-tech buyer base. Weak recurring mandatory workflow. Score 3.

Duty only partly confirmed. The 1909 law requires associations to keep a receipts-and-expenses ledger and show it on request. I could not confirm a set annual statement filing to the Interior Ministry, a format, or a penalty. Scholars say enforcement is laissez-faire. BDL Circular 170 exists, but the coverage I found concerns sanctioned bodies (Al-Qard Al-Hassan), not a general bank demand for NGO paperwork. I found no local product for Lebanese association filing (only generic Odoo, Vyapar, Qoyod). The 13,000 count is from the claim's Annahar link, which I could not open. Pain and willingness to pay are weak, and donor reporting is already served by generic fund-accounting tools. Score stays at 3.

The duty is real. The Beirut Governor (Marwan Abboud) gave unlicensed stations a "last" deadline of 31/12/2025, then extended it. The new date is not published in what I found. Each station must file a licence file with its municipality, with a report from an accredited technical audit office registered with an engineers' syndicate. The audit covers safety, tanks and fire protection. Decree 5509 sets 800 m spacing. The Energy Minister asked for illegal stations to be closed. Market: about 3,500 stations, roughly 1,500 non-compliant (estimate; the syndicate says no exact count exists). No competing software or state portal appeared in two Arabic searches, and the article mentions no digital system. Weaknesses: it is a one-off, enforcement is weak, the work is engineering and physical (tanks, spacing), and the real cost is the audit and the works, not the paperwork. Spacing may make many stations ineligible no matter what the file says. Recurrence is low and the buyer pool is small. I did not find the extension date, other governorates' notices, or audit fees.

result.competitor: No Lebanese guest-register product found. Generic foreign tools (eReg, GoCanvas, GuestBook, OtelMS) show no General Security integration. The state-run hotel reporting channel is unnamed. The official General Security app covers passports and residency, not hotels.
result.duty: Not confirmed in law. Annahar quotes the hotel syndicate head saying guest data is sent to Public Security on arrival. The guest-house syndicate circular demands reporting all guests. No legal basis, frequency or penalty found; it looks like a security-driven circular in 2026.
result.market: Not quantified. No register count found for hotels, guest houses or Airbnb hosts.
result.reason: Reports (Annahar, Mar 2026) say the hotel syndicate head states guest data goes to Public/General Security on arrival and the guest-house syndicate told members to report all guests. I found no statute, penalty or named app. The duty looks like a wartime circular, not a recurring statutory filing. The state already supplies the channel (an app or database), which leaves a vendor little to build except a thin PMS add-on, and no API is evidenced. Hotels also reportedly send data to Army Intelligence. The market is small and shrinking: Airbnb hosts are unregulated, and the guest-house syndicate has few members. No local competitor found, but the foreign PMS tools I saw (eReg, GoCanvas) are generic. Willingness to pay is weak, and the rules may lapse with the security situation. I did not fetch pages or search the Tourism Ministry rules.

Only one source (L'Orient Today, 403 on fetch; search snippets only) says Minister Lahoud gave unlicensed tourism businesses one year from publication to comply, then legal action. Decision text, date, penalty and number of businesses were not found. The UAE ban lift on 7 May suggests May 2026, so the deadline probably passed or was extended. Lahoud was still minister in July 2026 per Al-Modon. This is a one-off, with no recurring duty. Unlicensed operators are poor software buyers, and file preparation is a manual or consulting service. No competitor search found anything, but the market is weak. Nothing in the searches lets me size the market.

The duty is real: Art. 52 of the 2026 budget law and decision 616/1 of 29 June 2026 impose 17% on Sayrafa profits for 2021-23, with the threshold raised to USD 100,000. The deadline was 1 Oct 2026, and the ministry said in July and August there would be no extension. I found no later extension, but could not rule one out. It is a one-off duty and the deadline has passed. The population is small, wealthy individuals and companies, with no figure given. Demand is mostly accountants doing a one-time calculation, so the product is weak. I did not run a competitor search and the form names T5 and S18 are unverified. Penalties and the article-number conflict (2026 Art. 52 vs 2024 Art. 93) are unresolved.
